source_refs.note: Topic 22.1 with Quick Check 22.1, printed pages 86-87 (PDF 89-90). The book's 'alkyl or aryl group' is marked: -OH on an aryl carbon is a phenol.

blocks.text: Hydroxyl group (-OH) is the functional group of all alcohols. Alcohols are represented by the general formula ROH, where R is an alkyl or aryl group. The family also includes familiar substances as cholesterol and the carbohydrates. Methanol (CH₃OH) and ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) are the first two members of the homologous series of monohydric alcohols.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book says R in ROH may be an alkyl or aryl group. When the -OH group is bonded to an aryl (aromatic ring) carbon the compound is a phenol, not an alcohol, as the book itself says in its opening lines and in 22.5. In an alcohol, R is an alkyl group.
Depending on the number of hydroxyl groups attached, alcohols can be classified into monohydric and polyhydric alcohols.

blocks.alt: Four alcohols: ethanol CH3CH2OH and propan-1-ol CH3CH2CH2OH; 1,2-ethanediol (glycol), two CH2-OH units stacked; and 1,2,3-propanetriol (glycerol), CH2-OH, CH-OH and CH2-OH stacked.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed labels '1,2-ethandiol' and '1,2,3-propantriol' are misspelt; they are 1,2-ethanediol and 1,2,3-propanetriol.
Depending on the number of carbon atoms which are directly attached to the carbon that is bonded with the -OH group, alcohols can be classified into three types.

items: A primary (1°) alcohol is one in which the OH group is attached a primary carbon atom. Its general formula is R₁CH₂OH.
A secondary (2°) alcohol is one in which the OH group is attached to a secondary carbon atom. Its general formula is R₂CHOH.
A tertiary (3°) alcohol is one in which the OH group is attached a tertiary carbon atom. Its general formula is R₃COH.
